interactions.message: Warfarin + Aspirin: significantly increased bleeding risk. Monitor INR closely.
Warfarin + Ibuprofen: increased bleeding risk and GI bleed. Avoid combination.
Warfarin + Diclofenac: increased bleeding risk. Avoid combination.
Warfarin + Metronidazole: increased anticoagulant effect. Monitor INR.
Warfarin + Fluconazole: increased anticoagulant effect. Reduce warfarin dose and monitor INR.
Metformin + Insulin: increased hypoglycemia risk. Monitor blood glucose closely.
ACE inhibitor + NSAID: reduced antihypertensive effect and increased renal risk. Monitor BP and creatinine.
ACE inhibitor + NSAID: reduced antihypertensive effect and increased renal risk. Monitor BP and creatinine.
Ciprofloxacin + Metronidazole: increased QT prolongation risk. Use with caution, monitor ECG if available.
Corticosteroid + NSAID: increased GI bleed risk. Add gastroprotection (omeprazole).
Tramadol + Morphine: additive CNS depression. Risk of respiratory depression.
Simvastatin + Azithromycin: increased risk of rhabdomyolysis. Monitor for muscle pain.
Rifampicin + Oral contraceptives: rifampicin significantly reduces contraceptive efficacy. Use alternative contraception (IUD, depot injection).
Rifampicin + Levonorgestrel: rifampicin significantly reduces contraceptive efficacy. Use alternative contraception (IUD, depot injection).
Rifampicin + Warfarin: rifampicin drastically reduces warfarin levels. Need 2-5x warfarin dose increase. Monitor INR closely.
Rifampicin + Nevirapine: AVOID combination. Rifampicin reduces nevirapine levels by 20-58%. Use efavirenz-based ART regimen instead.
Rifampicin + Dolutegravir: rifampicin reduces dolutegravir levels. Double dolutegravir dose to 50mg BID during TB treatment.
Rifampicin + Efavirenz: moderate interaction. Efavirenz 600mg daily is standard — no dose adjustment usually needed. Monitor virological response.
Rifampicin + Lopinavir/ritonavir: CONTRAINDICATED. Rifampicin reduces lopinavir levels by >75%. Use rifabutin or switch ART.
Rifampicin + Atazanavir: CONTRAINDICATED. Rifampicin drastically reduces atazanavir levels. Switch to efavirenz-based ART.
Isoniazid + Phenytoin: isoniazid inhibits phenytoin metabolism, causing toxicity (ataxia, nystagmus). Monitor phenytoin levels.
Isoniazid + Carbamazepine: isoniazid inhibits carbamazepine metabolism. Risk of toxicity. Monitor levels.
Pyrazinamide + Allopurinol: both affect uric acid levels. Pyrazinamide causes hyperuricemia. Monitor uric acid and adjust allopurinol.
Efavirenz + Diazepam: efavirenz inhibits diazepam metabolism, causing prolonged sedation. Use lorazepam or oxazepam instead.
Atazanavir + Omeprazole/PPIs: PPIs reduce atazanavir absorption by >75%. AVOID combination. Use H2-blocker (ranitidine) if needed.
Zidovudine + Stavudine: pharmacologically ANTAGONISTIC. Never combine these two NRTIs.
Tenofovir + NSAIDs: additive nephrotoxicity risk. Avoid prolonged NSAID use. Monitor renal function.
Tenofovir + NSAIDs: additive nephrotoxicity risk. Avoid prolonged NSAID use. Monitor renal function.
Artemether-Lumefantrine + Erythromycin: increased QT prolongation risk. Monitor for cardiac symptoms.
Quinine + Digoxin: quinine increases digoxin levels. Halve digoxin dose during quinine treatment. Monitor for digoxin toxicity.
Metronidazole + Alcohol: disulfiram-like reaction (severe nausea, vomiting, flushing, tachycardia). Avoid alcohol during and 48hrs after treatment.
ACE inhibitor + Spironolactone: risk of severe hyperkalemia. Monitor potassium within 1 week of starting. Avoid if K+ >5.0.
ACE inhibitor + Spironolactone: risk of severe hyperkalemia. Monitor potassium within 1 week of starting.
Aminoglycoside + Loop diuretic: additive ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity. Avoid combination if possible. Monitor renal function and hearing.
Fluoroquinolone + Iron: iron reduces ciprofloxacin absorption by up to 90%. Take ciprofloxacin 2hrs before or 6hrs after iron.
Fluoroquinolone + Calcium/Antacids: reduced ciprofloxacin absorption. Take ciprofloxacin 2hrs before or 6hrs after.
Digoxin + Amiodarone: amiodarone increases digoxin levels by 70-100%. Halve digoxin dose when starting amiodarone.
Lithium + NSAIDs: NSAIDs reduce lithium clearance, causing toxicity. Avoid combination or monitor lithium levels closely.
SSRI + Tramadol: risk of serotonin syndrome (agitation, tremor, hyperthermia). Avoid combination if possible.
Methotrexate + TMP-SMX: bone marrow suppression and pancytopenia risk. AVOID combination. Monitor FBC if unavoidable.
Phenytoin + Oral contraceptives: phenytoin reduces contraceptive efficacy. Use higher-dose pill or alternative contraception.
Carbamazepine + Oral contraceptives: carbamazepine reduces contraceptive efficacy. Use alternative contraception.
Theophylline + Ciprofloxacin: ciprofloxacin inhibits theophylline metabolism. Risk of theophylline toxicity (seizures, arrhythmia).
Methyldopa + Iron: iron reduces methyldopa absorption. Take 2 hours apart.
TMP-SMX + Warfarin: TMP-SMX increases warfarin effect. Risk of bleeding. Monitor INR closely.
Fluconazole + Simvastatin: increased statin levels, risk of rhabdomyolysis. Suspend statin during fluconazole course.
Corticosteroid + NSAID: increased GI bleed risk. Add gastroprotection (omeprazole).
Amitriptyline + Tramadol: increased seizure risk and serotonin syndrome. Avoid combination.
Two antipsychotics: additive sedation, QT prolongation, and extrapyramidal effects. Use single agent when possible.
Glibenclamide + Fluconazole: fluconazole increases sulfonylurea levels. Risk of severe hypoglycemia. Monitor glucose closely.
AL + Efavirenz: efavirenz reduces artemether levels. Monitor for treatment failure. Consider extending AL course if response poor.
